answer.cloud design system

The default brand style guide for answer.cloud sites. A restrained, technical, and editorial system for AI, infrastructure, and developer-focused products — built on a compact type scale, a structured grid, and intentional use of blue.

Explore tokens Component preview
01
Foundations

Brand overview

answer.cloud is an answer engine for technical products. The visual language is quiet and precise: it should feel intelligent and functional, closer to a reference manual than a marketing page. Content sits directly on the page, aligned to a strong grid, separated by thin rules rather than cards.

Use this system as the default starting point for any answer.cloud site. It favors left-aligned, multi-column information layouts, generous but controlled whitespace, and a deliberate, sparing use of accent blue.

VoiceTechnical, exact
DensityHigh, readable
ToneEditorial
02
Foundations

Design principles

01

Structure over decoration

Hierarchy comes from grid, weight, spacing, and thin rules — not shadows or ornament.

02

Restrained typography

A compact scale that never exceeds 32px. Confidence through precision, not size.

03

Intentional blue

Accent reserved for actions, selection, links, and focus. Everything else stays neutral.

04

Editorial, not promotional

Left-aligned, information-dense layouts that read like technical documentation.

Typography

Primary typeface
Instrument Sans

Used for headings, body, navigation, labels, buttons, and interface. A monospace (JetBrains Mono) is reserved for code, commands, status values, and metadata.

Regular 400 Medium 500 Semibold 600 Mono 400/500
Rules
  • Never exceed 32px.
  • Keep heading steps small; use weight and rules for hierarchy.
  • Sentence case for headings; uppercase only for small labels.
  • Left-align headings; keep comfortable reading widths.
  • Subtle negative tracking on headings only.

Grid & background treatments

Technical grid

Thin, low-contrast, fades at edges. Behind selected sections only.

grid.css
--grid-line: rgba(26, 27, 28, 0.08);

background-image:
  linear-gradient(var(--grid-line) 1px, transparent 1px),
  linear-gradient(90deg, var(--grid-line) 1px, transparent 1px);
background-size: 140px 160px;

23
Visual assets

Images & figures

Use images and figures as structured editorial content — to support explanation, evidence, product understanding, or technical storytelling. Every visual has a clear purpose; none is decorative filler.

Favor
  • Documentary & architectural imagery
  • Close-up technical detail, texture, scale
  • Product interface captures & annotated screenshots
  • Research diagrams, schematics, data visualizations
  • Abstract composition with restrained color
Avoid
  • Generic stock & smiling office teams
  • Artificially futuristic AI, glowing brains, humanoid robots
  • Neon circuitry, holograms, decorative 3D blobs
  • Heavy filters, duotones, neon grading
  • Images used only to fill empty space
Corners0–4px
Border1px · rgba(26,27,28,.12)
Shadownone
Alignmentto page grid
Full-bleedsparingly

Images sit flush with adjacent rules and columns — square or rectangular, thin-bordered when separation is needed, never floating rounded cards with heavy drop shadows.

25
Visual assets

Figures

Treat diagrams, charts, screenshots, and visual explanations as formal figures with a consistent structure: label, title, visual, caption, and source.

Two-column figure

Text beside imagery

The editorial default: a reading column paired with a supporting figure of equal weight. The figure keeps a natural proportion and aligns to the same baseline as the text.

See figure anatomy
Structure
Fig. 00Label · 11–12px · uppercase · muted
Descriptive title14–16px · medium · ink

Source / attributionmono · caption
27
Visual assets

Diagrams & schematics

Thin lines, simple geometry, clear directional arrows, minimal color. Accent blue marks the active path; muted gray carries secondary relationships. Diagrams read like technical documentation, not marketing infographics.

28
Visual assets

Data visualizations

Restrained and highly readable. Ink for primary data, accent blue for the point that matters, muted gray for secondary series, thin grid lines, direct labels, and one clear message per chart. No rainbow palettes, 3D, or decorative backgrounds.

For processes and product walkthroughs, use numbered steps separated by dividers — not floating cards. Each step: number, short title, figure, one concise explanation.

Grids, background & color treatment

Detail paired with wider context

Background image · text beside, not over
Research

Grounding at scale

Text sits in a quiet region over a subtle overlay, kept compact with verified contrast. On mobile it moves below the image.

Use background imagery sparingly — prefer placing text beside imagery rather than over it, and never set long paragraphs over a photograph.

Accessibility rules
  • Meaningful images carry descriptive alt text.
  • Decorative images use empty alt="".
  • Figures include captions when context isn't obvious.
  • Charts & diagrams provide a text summary and key values.
  • Status uses non-color indicators, not hue alone.
  • Essential information never lives only inside an image.
